name: sql
title: SQL
description: Perform SQL queries using Spring JDBC.
label: database

properties.name: query
properties.description: Sets the SQL query to perform. You can externalize the query by using file: or classpath: as prefix and specify the location of the file.

properties.name: allowNamedParameters
properties.description: Whether to allow using named parameters in the queries.

properties.name: dataSource
properties.description: Sets the DataSource to use to communicate with the database at endpoint level.

properties.name: outputClass
properties.description: Specify the full package and class name to use as conversion when outputType=SelectOne.

properties.name: outputHeader
properties.description: Store the query result in a header instead of the message body. By default, outputHeader == null and the query result is stored in the message body, any existing content in the message body is discarded. If outputHeader is set, the value is used as the name of the header to store the query result and the original message body is preserved.

properties.name: outputType
properties.description: Make the output of consumer or producer to SelectList as List of Map, or SelectOne as single Java object in the following way: a) If the query has only single column, then that JDBC Column object is returned. (such as SELECT COUNT( ) FROM PROJECT will return a Long object. b) If the query has more than one column, then it will return a Map of that result. c) If the outputClass is set, then it will convert the query result into an Java bean object by calling all the setters that match the column names. It will assume your class has a default constructor to create instance with. d) If the query resulted in more than one rows, it throws an non-unique result exception. StreamList streams the result of the query using an Iterator. This can be used with the Splitter EIP in streaming mode to process the ResultSet in streaming fashion.

properties.name: separator
properties.description: The separator to use when parameter values is taken from message body (if the body is a String type), to be inserted at # placeholders. Notice if you use named parameters, then a Map type is used instead. The default value is comma

properties.name: breakBatchOnConsumeFail
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets whether to break batch if onConsume failed.

properties.name: expectedUpdateCount
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets an expected update count to validate when using onConsume.

properties.name: maxMessagesPerPoll
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets the maximum number of messages to poll

properties.name: onConsume
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: After processing each row then this query can be executed, if the Exchange was processed successfully, for example to mark the row as processed. The query can have parameter.

properties.name: onConsumeBatchComplete
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: After processing the entire batch, this query can be executed to bulk update rows etc. The query cannot have parameters.

properties.name: onConsumeFailed
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: After processing each row then this query can be executed, if the Exchange failed, for example to mark the row as failed. The query can have parameter.

properties.name: routeEmptyResultSet
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets whether empty resultset should be allowed to be sent to the next hop. Defaults to false. So the empty resultset will be filtered out.

properties.name: sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

properties.name: transacted
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Enables or disables transaction. If enabled then if processing an exchange failed then the consumer breaks out processing any further exchanges to cause a rollback eager.

properties.name: useIterator
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets how resultset should be delivered to route. Indicates delivery as either a list or individual object. defaults to true.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: pollStrategy
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

properties.name: processingStrategy
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows to plugin to use a custom org.apache.camel.component.sql.SqlProcessingStrategy to execute queries when the consumer has processed the rows/batch.

properties.name: batch
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Enables or disables batch mode

properties.name: batchAutoCommitDisabled
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Whether to optimize batch by turning off auto-commit which can dramatic improve performance, and instead execute as a manual commit after the entire batch operation is complete

properties.name: noop
properties.label: producer
properties.description: If set, will ignore the results of the SQL query and use the existing IN message as the OUT message for the continuation of processing

properties.name: useMessageBodyForSql
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Whether to use the message body as the SQL and then headers for parameters. If this option is enabled then the SQL in the uri is not used. Note that query parameters in the message body are represented by a question mark instead of a # symbol.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: alwaysPopulateStatement
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If enabled then the populateStatement method from org.apache.camel.component.sql.SqlPrepareStatementStrategy is always invoked, also if there is no expected parameters to be prepared. When this is false then the populateStatement is only invoked if there is 1 or more expected parameters to be set; for example this avoids reading the message body/headers for SQL queries with no parameters.

properties.name: fetchSize
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Gives the JDBC driver a hint as to the number of rows that should be fetched from the database when more rows are needed for ResultSet objects generated by this Statement. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored. The default value is zero. This is important for processing large result sets: Setting this higher than the default value will increase processing speed at the cost of memory consumption; setting this lower can avoid transferring row data that will never be read by the application.

properties.name: parametersCount
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If set greater than zero, then Camel will use this count value of parameters to replace instead of querying via JDBC metadata API. This is useful if the JDBC vendor could not return correct parameters count, then user may override instead.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Specifies a character that will be replaced to in SQL query. Notice, that it is simple String.replaceAll() operation and no SQL parsing is involved (quoted strings will also change).

properties.name: prepareStatementStrategy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Allows to plugin to use a custom org.apache.camel.component.sql.SqlPrepareStatementStrategy to control preparation of the query and prepared statement.

properties.name: rowMapperFactory
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Factory for creating RowMapper

properties.name: templateOptions
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Configures the Spring JdbcTemplate with the key/values from the Map. This is a multi-value option with prefix: template.

properties.name: usePlaceholder
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Sets whether to use placeholder and replace all placeholder characters with sign in the SQL queries.

properties.name: backoffErrorThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffIdleThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffMultiplier
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

properties.name: delay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the next poll.

properties.name: greedy
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

properties.name: initialDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

properties.name: repeatCount
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

properties.name: runLoggingLevel
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

properties.name: scheduledExecutorService
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

properties.name: scheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

properties.name: schedulerProperties
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

properties.name: startScheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

properties.name: timeUnit
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

properties.name: useFixedDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.
